{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "jeanpablojp",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK, but raised issues with temp dir handling, crash reporting under failure, coverage loss, and setup overhead"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "r:5067237541",
      "kind": "approach",
      "harm": "targets with heavy per-input initialization incur higher cumulative execution time when sharded across processes",
      "quote": "utxo_total_supply builds a ChainTestingSetup inside the target body, so a datadir per input, and three shards of 680 take around 240s each against 200s for all 2040 in one process.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "c:5491605174"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "c:5496330017",
      "settled_by_quote": "You're right. utxo_total_supply is the last to finish in all 20 master runs I checked, and it runs for the last 86 to 214s of them, so my sentence was wrong."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3895026578",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "temporary directory creation fails when parent directory is read-only even without sharding, and directories survive SIGTERM",
      "quote": "with a read-only parent the run dies in mkdtemp, and --corpus-shards 1 doesn't avoid it. It also survives a SIGTERM, left next to the corpus.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3902537554"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3902537554",
      "settled_by_quote": "fixed this in the latest push by having a temp dir for each job"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3895026588",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "harm": "exiting on failure removes shard directories while other shards run, causing remaining shards to fail on read_file assertions instead of the real error",
      "quote": "with the sys.exit(1) in here, the dir disappears under the shards that are still running, so on the standalone builds they die on the read_file Assert instead of on the input that actually broke.",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3902537218"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3902537218",
      "settled_by_quote": "I guess this is fixed by having per-job tmp dirs for the shards."
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:3895026591",
      "kind": "interface",
      "harm": "fuzz coverage metrics become per-process rather than per-target, preventing comparison of aggregate coverage across commits",
      "quote": "cov: becomes per process... you can't compare coverage across a change any more. Could the shards be folded back into one line per target?",
      "blocking": false,
      "status": "resolved",
      "author_replies": [
        "rc:3902536977"
      ],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "settled_by_id": "rc:3902536977",
      "settled_by_quote": "I don't think it is possible to recover the coverage from the shards. I can only see compiling with coverage instrumentation and then using that."
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "r:5067237541",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "On Windows and MSan where runtime is dominated by single long targets, sharding cuts the tail latency and yields clear wins.",
      "substantive": true
    }
  ],
  "notes": "Initial assessment tracking jeanpablojp's Concept ACK and several resolved non-blocking concerns regarding tempdir handling, crash masking, coverage metric reporting, and target setup overhead."
}
